words.definition:
Retention of your own culture within a minority community in a country while also adapting some aspect of the majority culture.
In their sociology class, the students studied the difference between assimilation and acculturation.

Having no leader or chief.
In anthropology studies, the students learned that most foraging or wood- gatherer societies were acephalous.

Anonymous literary works, especially ancient Greek poetry.
Researchers studied adespota to gain knowledge from much earlier times.

A group of primitive, jawless vertebrates.
Jawless fish like lampreys and hagfish, members of the Agnatha class, also lack fins and stomachs.

Inability to process sensory information, usually as a result of brain damage.
The three main types of agnosia are visual, auditory, and tactile.

A grove of ailanthus trees.
The ailanthery was intended to provide food for silkworms.

An antigen present in some but not all individuals of the same species, as those in different blood types.
Researchers discovered that an alloantigen stimulates the immune system of the host against foreign antigens.

Any of the millions of tiny air sacs of the lungs.
Each alveolus is wrapped in a fine mesh of capillaries.

A white linen cloth worn on the neck and shoulders by a priest.
The word amice comes from a Latin word meaning wrapped around.

A group of minerals forming prism or needle-like crystals.
The contractor used amphibole for paving stones and as a veneer on buildings.

A clearly old-fashioned thing.
In today’s computer world, a floppy disk is an anachronism.

Relating to or requiring an absence of free oxygen.
Below the depth of oxygen penetration, life is restricted to anaerobic bacteria.

Referring to a pain-relieving drug.
The patient’s sprained wrist was treated with a sling and analgesic medication.

A state of disorder due to absence or non-recognition of authority.
When you have people losing trust in the system, it leads to anarchy.

A formal act whereby a country, state or city proclaims its sovereignty over territory hitherto outside its domain.
The area of the city was greatly increased by its annexation of the suburbs.

A fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, usually for the rest of one’s life.
The pensioner was happy to have an annuity which paid him a guaranteed income for the rest of his life.

Referring to identifying details having been removed.
The computer expert anonymized the data so that the original source would not be revealed.

Occurring in the hours before dawn.
The tired doctor returned from his house call in the gloomy antelucan hour.

An ornamental design of alternating motifs resembling clusters of narrow leaves.
The decorator stencilled an anthemion motif on a small section of the wall, so the homeowner could see it and decide whether or not to continue.

Referring to environmental pollution resulting from human activity.
Excessive greenhouse emissions are anthropogenic.

The study of human societies and cultures.
Ethnography is a research approach developed in anthropology to study small-group culture.

The attribution of human characteristics or behaviour to a god, animal, or object.
Pet owners are inclined towards anthropomorphism.

A substance that interferes with the normal metabolic processes within cells.
Gout is treated with an antimetabolite.

Giving rise to anxiety.
Caffeine is an anxiogenic agent as it can cause a person to feel nervous.

The main clause of a conditional sentence.
The apodosis is often contrasted with the protasis.

Not interested or involved in politics.
Our neighbour is an apolitical type who doesn’t usually vote.

Referring to markings or colourings used to repel or warn predators.
The bright colours of poison arrow frogs and some butterflies are aposematic protection.

Divided up and shared.
They met with the estate lawyer to find out how their father’s money was apportioned in his will.

Extreme or irrational fear of spiders.
Because of her arachnophobia, she is frightened whenever she sees a spider.

Referring to plants growing in sand.
Peanuts are arenaceous plants, growing best in sandy soil.

Referring to rocks or sediment consisting of or containing clay.
Shale and slate are argillaceous rocks.

To take or claim something without justification.
It is hard to watch the attempts of a world leader trying to arrogate powers that aren’t his.

Referring to the upward movement of water under natural pressure.
An artesian well is a water well that does not require a pump to bring water to the surface.

A person who physically attacks another.
The victim was unable to describe the assailant because the mugging was over in seconds.

Melancholy or irritable.
Peers usually avoid a person with an atrabilious temperment.

Reduced in force, effect, or value.
Earplugs attenuated the loud sounds of the machinery.

A poem or piece of music appropriate to the dawn or early morning.
An aubade is the opposite of a serenade, which is intended for performance in the evening.

Being a sign of future success.
Some people think that the start of the year is an auspicious time to make resolutions.

Commanding and self-confident; likely to be respected and obeyed.
The calm, authoritative voice restored order in the chaotic classroom.

Providing additional help and support.
The homeowner bought a generator as an auxiliary power source in case the electricity went out.

A wine barrel.
The vintner aged the wine for two years in an oak barrique.

A person who walks along a beach looking for interesting items.
The beachcomber collected driftwood to make unique furniture.

A dance of Caribbean origin, similar to the foxtrot.
At night, party-goers dance the beguine.

A branch of science concerned with the biological processes involved in aging.
The interdisciplinary research of biogerontology studies the causes, effects, and mechanisms of aging.

The application of statistical analysis to biological data.
Mathematically trained, the biologist was interested in both systemics and biometry.

A surgical knife.
A bistoury can be used for surgery, for podiatry, and for arts and crafts.

Small balls of mozzarella cheese.
Traditional Caprese salad has fresh bocconcini cheese, ripe tomatoes, and basil.

The visual quality of the out-of-focus areas of a photographic image.
The photographer used bokeh for the background to make the subject in the foreground stand out.

A rumbling or gurgling noise made by the movement of fluid and gas in the intestines.
Drinking water can help stop borborygmus.

An instrument used to inspect the inside of a structure through a small hole.
A borescope inspection of the engine showed no visible damage.

A harsh discordant mixture of sounds.
Birds form a group and create a cacophony of sound to ward off attacks.

A small hybrid fruit-bearing plant.
While calamansi is native to the Philippines, it is grown in Canada as a tropical houseplant.

A plant that grows best in calcium-rich soil.
The honeysuckle vine draped over the fence was a beautiful sample of a calcicole.

One of the D vitamins.
Vitamin D, also called calciferol, is referred to as the sunshine vitamin because the body can manufacture this vitamin from sunlight absorbed by your skin.

Eyeshadow.
It is much easier to say “eyeshadow” than to pronounce the original name, calliblephary, for colouring for eyelids.

A picture made of words; a shaped poem.
In Alice in Wonderland, ‘The Mouse’s Tale’ is a fun calligram because it is written to look like a mouse’s tail curling across the page.

The borrowing of a word or phrase from another language and literally translated and then used in another way.
An ‘Adam’s apple’ is a calque, or loan translation, of the French ‘pomme d’Adam’.

A short, light vocal piece of music.
The canzonetta is a style of vocal music that flourished in the late 16th and early 17th centuries.

Having the potential to cause cancer.
Because asbestos is carcinogenic, workers removing it wear protective clothing.

Unambiguously explicit and direct.
The doctor said it was a categorical truth that masks help control the spread of COVID-19.

A person who is a hundred or more years old.
The senior home arranged a lovely birthday party for the centenarian.

A slipper.
A chappal is similar to a sandal.

A series of discordant noises.
He played a charivari on the piano to express his anger.

A soft, smooth silky dress fabric.
With its drape, charmeuse works well for blouses, scarves, and lingerie.

Displaying prejudiced support for one’s own cause, group, or sex.
We all need to combat stereotypes and chauvinistic attitudes.

The pincer-like claws of some crustaceans or arachnids.
Ticks have modified chelicerae for piercing.

A fear of chemicals, especially as used in artificial food products.
To understand chemophobia, we must be aware that scientists and the general public see risks differently.

A large sheep of a breed with short, thick wool.
The wool of a Cheviot is known for its durability.

A small deerlike mammal with tusks.
A chevrotain, a shy, nocturnal vegetarian, is the smallest hoofed mammal in the world.

A literary device in which words or concepts are repeated in reverse order.
A simple way to add emphasis is to use a chiasmus, such as ‘Never let a fool kiss you or a kiss fool you.’

A free-standing clay fireplace or oven that has a bulbous, hollow body connected to a narrow smoke vent.
The landscaper suggested adding a chimenea to their small garden for heat on cool evenings.

Handwriting or penmanship.
The lady used chirography to create beautiful thank-you notes.

Non-toxic, non-flammable chemicals.
The manufacturers of aerosol sprays, solvents, and refrigerants used chlorofluorocarbons before we became aware of the danger they posed to the ozone layer.

A structure in plant cells which contains chlorophyll and in which photosynthesis takes place.
The chloroplast in a plant allows it to capture the energy of the sun in energy-rich molecules.

A Eurasian and North African bird of the crow family.
While its black plumage identifies it as a crow, the chough has a red bill and legs unlike any other member of the crow family.

A tangerine of a deep orange-red North African variety.
A clementine is a citrus fruit.

A projecting corner or angle of a wall.
The red granite coign of each corner was a beautiful contrast to the grey walls.

To divide into separate sections or categories.
The psychologist said the ability to compartmentalize is a defense mechanism or coping strategy.

The scientific study of shells.
The director of the Shell Museum wrote several books on conchology.

An extinct fossil marine animal of the Cambrian to Triassic periods.
The conodont resembled a modern- day eel.

The fact of being descended from the same ancestor.
Both a social and genetic concept, their consanguinity meant that the cousins had a high chance of inheriting the same blood disorder their grandfather had.

Attracting notice or attention.
The shy clown felt conspicuous in his bright costume.

Giving rise or likely to give rise to controversy or public disagreement.
At the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, the issue of wearing masks was controversial.

The process of changing, or causing something to change, from one form to another.
One farm is about to achieve organic status, and another is in the process of conversion.

Collaboration between business competitors, in the hope of mutually beneficial results.
The market analyst wrote about the concept of coopetition.

A funeral song of Scottish or Irish origin.
The bagpiper played a sombre coronach.

Extreme or irrational fear of clowns.
Sufferers of coulrophobia agree that the heavy makeup, big nose, and weird hair colour are all fear-inducing.

The skull, especially the part enclosing the brain.
The cranium supports the structure of the face and forms a protective cavity for the brain.

Principles or standards by which something may be judged.
A green label indicates the product has met certain environmental criteria.

An area of land attached to a house and forming one enclosure with it.
When it comes to property, curtilage is an important legal concept.

The practice of monitoring digital data relating to personal details or online activities.
Mass dataveillance threatens us with invasion of privacy.

To officially remove an item from a library, museum, or art gallery to sell it.
The museum will deaccession this painting to buy other works.

A meeting to discuss a completed undertaking.
The purpose of the debriefing was to encourage reflection and build improvement into future plans.

Lying flat; horizontal.
In botany, a decumbent plant lies along the ground with the extremity curving upwards.

Uncooperative or non-compliant.
The mood of the protestors was defiant.

The quality of being delicate or tactful.
The grandmother’s delicatesse endeared her to many.

A lustrous green gemstone.
A demantoid is a member of the garnet family.

Relating to the kind of language used by ordinary people.
The author wrote his novel in a vivid demotic style.

A desperate or reckless person, especially a criminal.
The historical novel series featuring a daring desperado has given way to a new series of Western movies.

A cause of harm or damage.
The excuse-making in the meeting was a detriment to productive discussion.

A roadside food stall.
For mouth-watering rotis, the dhaba by the college was highly recommended.

The two dots placed over a vowel to indicate that it is sounded separately, such as in the surname Brontë.
The diaeresis is seldom seen nowadays, as many editors no longer insist on its use.

A gap between a person’s two front teeth.
Dentists use the word diastema to describe the gap between two teeth.

An Australian Aboriginal wind instrument.
A didgeridoo, shaped like a long wooden tube, produces a deep, resonant sound when blown.

A person who cultivates an area of interest, such as the arts, without real commitment or knowledge.
Self-discipline separates the true student from the dilettante.

A decrease in loudness in a piece of music.
The music swelled to a crescendo, then dissipated with a diminuendo.

A reduction in size, extent or importance of something.
The second wave indicated the pandemic showed no signs of diminution.

To free from a burden.
A day at the spa helped the harried executive disencumber herself of the job’s frustrations.

Not candid or sincere.
Because the journalist pretended to know less than he admitted, he was described as disingenuous and untrustworthy.

Exemption from a rule or usual requirement.
Rules on taxation may include dispensation for charitable organizations.

Rock consisting of dolomite, an important industrial mineral.
A walk over the property turned up layers of promising dolostone.

A member of a crew trained for underground rescue work.
The draegerman wore a breathing apparatus to go into the hazardous situation and rescue the miners.

A sweet or pleasing manner of speaking.
The dulciloquy of her heroine was a tone the novelist was trying to establish.

In ecology, referring to a lake with brown acidic water that is low in oxygen.
A dystrophic lake supports little life due to its acidic conditions.

A succulent plant with rosettes of fleshy colourful leaves.
The most important part of echeveria care is watering, as overwatering can cause rot.

The action of vomiting.
The drug allows you to control emesis resulting from motion sickness.

Each of a pair of molecules that are mirror images of each other.
Except for the direction of the rotation, enantiomers have identical chemical and physical properties.

An inflammation of the endocardium, which is a layer of tissue lining the chambers of the heart.
His life was in danger due to endocarditis.

A slight convex curve in the shaft of a column.
The temple pillars exhibit entasis, making it a good example of propositional beauty.

To entangle or trap.
Fairy-tale characters have to take care not to entrammel themselves.

In ballet, a jump during which the dancer repeatedly crosses the feet and beats them together.
The curtain rose on the ballet and the first entrechat electrified the audience.

The branch of biochemistry concerned with enzymes.
The science midterm included questions concerning enzymology.

Referring to plants growing on the surface of other plants.
An epiphytic plant is not parasitic on the supporting plant.

The natural or artificial growth of crystals on top of another crystal.
The crystal-growing kit allowed the children to experiment with epitaxy.

A carriage and horses with attendants.
In the historical novel, the colonel’s equipage was described in great detail.

Relating to plants of the heather family.
The soil for ericaceous plants must be acidic for them to thrive.

Evaluating other cultures according to preconceptions originating in one’s own culture.
The editor made efforts to address and correct ethnocentric biases in the text.

Relating to the system of geometry based on the work of Euclid, a Greek mathematician.
From 300 B.C. to the 19th century, Euclidean geometry was the standard.

To make a problem worse.
The exorbitant cost of land in urban areas only exacerbated the housing problem.

Serving to lessen the seriousness of a situation.
Library staff will waive fines where there are genuine extenuating circumstances.

Occurring optionally in response to circumstances rather than by nature.
An organism that can use oxygen for energy production but can also survive without oxygen is described as a facultative anaerobe.

Consisting of or containing starch.
Their diet was mainly farinaceous food such as bread, macaroni, and potatoes.

A very small woodwind instrument resembling a recorder.
A flageolet is sometimes called a tin whistle.

Like tufts of wool.
The first snows of winter lay thick and flocculent.

Decorated with floral designs.
The wedding dress was a fantastic floriated tulle creation.

Tiny marine creatures that form intricately shaped shells.
When foraminifera die, thick ocean- floor sediments are formed from their shells.

Relating to or denoting conflict within a single family or organization.
Some companies, previously very successful, failed because of fratricidal disagreements.

A dish of stewed or fried pieces of meat served in a thick white sauce.
Julia Child described a fricassee as being halfway between a sauté and a stew.

Referring to the severe and sudden onset of a disease.
The range of clinical presentations can vary from asymptomatic to fulminant disease.

A traditional pleated skirt-like garment, also referred to as a kilt, worn by men in the Balkans for military and ceremonial occasions.
In modern times, the fustanella is a part of Balkan folk dress.

The study of the physical features of the surface of the earth and their relation to its geological structure.
The researchers in the geomorphology department concentrated their studies on watersheds and in particular, fluvial processes in mountainous regions.

A digital printing process in which an ink-jet printer is used to produce a high-quality art print.
A computer performs millions of calculations to produce a giclee print.

The smooth part of the forehead above and between the eyebrows.
When you make facial expressions, the glabella is moved by the muscles of your forehead.

A parasitic freshwater larva which attaches itself by hooks and suckers to the fins or gills of fish.
Eventually, the glochidium leaves the fish, falls to the lake floor, and metamorphoses into an adult.

Relating to grammar, the rules of a language.
The student received a low mark on the essay because of several grammatical errors.

A dark coarse-grained sandstone containing more than 15 percent clay.
The construction industry uses greywacke for cement manufacturing.

A small nocturnal antelope.
The grysbok spends the day in the protective cover of tall grass or shrubs.

A type of lace.
Because of its elegance, the bridal salon used guipure in its stunning creations.

The largest of the falcons.
The gyrfalcon is found in Arctic regions and has several colours, one of which is mainly white.

Early French settlers in Canada.
Many of the early French habitants established small farms.

A bridle without a bit, operated by exerting pressure on a horse’s nose.
The hackamore is traditionally used as the horse progresses in its training.

A piece of armour.
The costume designer studied the history and development of the hauberk so the film’s depiction would be accurate.

A metric unit of capacity equal to one hundred litres.
The hectolitre is used especially for wine, beer, grain, and other agricultural produce.

A low evergreen shrub, also called a rock rose.
The gardener placed a helianthemum in the foundation planting because it is a perennial plant.

A plant in the daisy family.
Some kinds of helichrysum are grown to be dried because they retain their shape and colour so well.

A mainly woodland orchid.
The landscape designer planted a helleborine because it would grow in shade.

A parasitic worm.
A helminth can be transmitted through contaminated soil.

A disease characterized by the inflammation of the liver.
A common cause of hepatitis is a viral infection.

Government by seven rulers.
Anglo-Saxon England was originally a heptarchy of seven smaller kingdoms.

Relating to plants with non-woody stems.
In Canada, the above ground growth of herbaceous plants largely or totally dies back in winter.

A major art museum in St.
Petersburg, Russia. Catherine the Great started the collections in the Hermitage.

A Hindu spring festival.
A treasured keepsake was a book of poems documenting Holi celebrations.

The branch of science and technology concerned with the transport of liquids through pipes and channels.
The instructor explained that hydraulics work by using pressurized fluid to power an engine.

A quality of coziness that creates a feeling of contentment.
Remembering the weekends spent at his Danish grandmother’s house as a child brought forth a comforting sense of hygge.

Severe and prolonged vomiting.
Persistent hyperemesis can lead to dehydration.

Long-sightedness.
The fashion model wore contact lenses to correct hypermetropia.

A person who is abnormally anxious about their health.
The hypochondriac had extreme anxiety about his health, even though diagnostic tests showed there was nothing wrong.

Referring to the rhythm or meter established by the words, which have a short unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable in a poem.
Words such as “attain,” “portray,” and “describe “are all examples of the iambic pattern.

Relating to illness caused by medical treatment.
The prescription drugs caused side effects leading to iatrogenic disease.

A person who favours the veneration of religious icons.
Orthodox Christians during the eighth and ninth centuries took the iconodule position.

A type of volcanic rock.
The main component of an ignimbrite is pumice.

A large partly-bipedal herbivorous dinosaur.
The iguanodon was a pack animal, often foraging for leaves and berries within the protection of 3-4 others.

About to happen.
If the door is opened, the alarm will sound so the homeowners are alerted to any imminent danger.

Not sensible or restrained; excessive.
The motorist lost his driving license because of his immoderate drinking.

A fund used by a business for small items of expenditure and restored to a fixed amount periodically.
The petty cash is kept in the office on the imprest system.

The fact of originating or occurring naturally in a particular place.
The lawyer argued for the collective rights based on the indigeneity of the community.

Impossible to see or clearly distinguish.
The heavy fog made driving dangerous because of indiscernible vehicles.

Hardened.
The soil was indurated from prolonged drought.

Unable to act in a relaxed and natural way because of self-consciousness or mental restraint.
Too much criticism can throw a person off balance and make them inhibited.

A white leavened Ethiopian bread, made from teff flour.
The restaurant had spicy lentils and warm injera on its lunchtime menu.

Without physical sensation.
Diabetics often suffer from insensate fingers.

A tough outer protective layer, especially that of an animal or plant.
In seeds, the integument is a layer of tissue that develops into a seed coat.

Having or showing a lack of self- control.
Aristotle’s work on justice and fairness is the foundation of this quote; “For if the ruler is intemperate and unjust, how can he rule well?”

The action of making or becoming more concentrated.
The intensification of agriculture has resulted in large-scale farming but with fewer farmers.

A family of proteins generated naturally by the body’s immune system.
By altering cell membranes to deny entry or exit, interferons act against viruses in a variety of ways.

A pause between the acts of a play.
During the interlude, the audience reflected on what they had seen on stage in Act I.

To mix or merge together.
Group and individual identities can interpenetrate and influence each other.

The rise and fall of the voice in speaking.
The rising intonation made the statement into a question.

Details, especially of a complicated or perplexing subject.
The political scientist student was interested in the intricacies of policy.

In a way that cannot be undone or put right.
Due to COVID-19, billions of dollars were irretrievably lost from the world economy.

A large Central and South American stork.
Tramping through the marshes of Costa Rica, the ornithologists identified the jabiru by its black neck, white plumage, and black bill.

A communal uprising or revolt.
Surprisingly, this time the jacquerie was started and maintained by women.

An Indian sweet.
The jalebi, made of a coil of batter fried and steeped in syrup, was the favourite choice on the dessert table.

The state or period of being young.
People who have reclaimed their juvenescence appear very happy.

A scrambling shrub with prickly stems and bright flowers, also known as the common lantana.
The horticulturalist collected seeds of the kayakeet.

The largest country in Central Asia.
Russia is on the northern boundary of Kazakhstan.

A paradoxical anecdote or riddle without a solution.
The koan is used in Zen Buddhism to demonstrate the inadequacy of logical reasoning and provoke enlightenment.

Something that can seriously weaken or harm a particular person or thing.
Flip-flopping on issues can be kryptonite to political candidates.

Inflammation of the inner ear.
The symptoms of labyrinthitis are dizziness, nausea, and loss of hearing.

Decorative articles, typically made of wood coated with lacquer.
Today, Japanese lacquerware can be found in various shapes, colours, and sizes in artisan shops.

The protein component of milk.
The allergist tested the patient for lactoprotein intolerance.

A destructive mudflow on the slopes of a volcano.
The dangerous lahar flowed down the river valley, far beyond the volcano.

Inflammation inside the hoof in horses and other animals.
Both the pony and the donkey suffered from extreme lameness caused by laminitis.

Referring to a hare; rabbit-like.
During story time, the librarian read about Peter Rabbit, the rebel of the leporine world.

In Irish folklore, a small, mischievous sprite.
The folklorist loved the myths and magic of Ireland, especially the idea of the leprechaun.

An ornamental initial letter larger than the rest of the text it accompanies.
The printer enjoyed the emphasis of using a lettrine to begin each paragraph.

A strong south-westerly wind blowing on the sea to the west of Italy.
The libeccio frequently raises high seas resulting in violent squalls.

To remove or loosen restrictions.
During the pandemic, governments decided to liberalize regulations about restaurant patios.

Relating to the combined motions or effects of the sun and moon.
Easter is determined on the basis of lunisolar cycles.

To freeze-dry something.
The growers use a manufacturer to lyophilize their coffee beans.

A stony coral.
The madrepore form reefs or islands in tropical locations.

The protective magnetic shield part of earth’s atmosphere.
About fifty years ago, a Canadian physicist showed how solar winds buffeted and shaped the earth’s magnetosphere.

In South Asia, an open space in or near a town, used as a parade ground or for events such as public meetings.
The town held cultural programmes and performances in the maidan.

A person who guarantees that another (especially a prisoner) will fulfil a legal obligation to appear in court on a specified day.
In the historical novel, the mainpernor was listed, along with other illustrious personages, as being a guarantor that the prisoner would be in court as requested.

Historically, a customary payment in the form of loaves of bread.
The mainport was made in recompense for tithes.

Brown cane that is used for walking sticks and umbrella handles.
While ash wood makes the strongest canes, the customer preferred the mottled brown of a malacca cane.

Not adjusting appropriately to the environment or situation.
Avoidance, withdrawal, and passive aggression are examples of maladaptive behaviours.

A root vegetable growing in tropical regions.
The Caribbean farmer grew malanga for its edible pear-shaped tubers.

A historical term for release from slavery.
The history student learned that when masters freed their slaves voluntarily, it was called manumission.

An author’s handwritten or typed text that has not yet been published.
There are more manuscripts available for publication than there are publishers willing to pay for them.

A person who suffers delusions of their own power or importance.
It was difficult for the diplomats to negotiate with the power-hungry megalomaniac.

An extinct giant ground sloth.
The paleontologists found evidence that a megatherium had lived on this island.

The belief that the world can be made better by human effort.
Faith in scientific and social meliorism sustains people’s optimism.

In Hawaii, a member of a mythical race of small people capable of great feats of construction.
Hawaiian legend has it that many centuries ago a menehune lived in this forest.

The curved upper surface of a liquid in a tube.
The scientist took great care reading the meniscus on a thermometer to determine the precise reading.

The solid upright section of a fort.
The narrow opening or tiny window in a merlon is called an “embrasure slit.”

The middle of three parts of a mollusc foot or of a leaf.
Another name for the mesopodium of a leaf is the petiole.

An era comprising the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods.
The Mesozoic era was also known as the age of dinosaurs.

The ability of chameleons and some other creatures to change colour to match their surroundings.
Metachrosis is common in vertebrates such as fish, amphibians, and some types of lizards.

The conversion to the metric system of measurement.
Canada’s metrication began in the 1970s.

A system of feudal land tenure where the farmer paid part of the farm’s produce as rent.
Some historians think the system of mezzadria, which was gradually discontinued after WWII, is responsible for the agricultural development of central Italy.

A component of limestone.
As well as having an extremely fine- grained texture, micrite is dull and opaque.

One thousandth of a second.
The burst of light from a camera flash lasts about one millisecond.

A sweet yellow fruit in the plum family.
During the family outing to a pick- your-own fruit farm, the child tried a mirabelle for the first time.

Historically, a shot fired from a cannon.
Fragments of scrap iron were used to form the mitraille.

A building or buildings occupied by a community of monks living under religious vows.
Scholarship and religious devotion were practised in the monastery.

Referring to being descended from a common evolutionary ancestor.
Well known monophyletic groups include all fur-bearing and feathered vertebrates.

The branch of study concerned with large topographic features of the earth’s surface, such as continents, mountain ranges and river basins.
Three branches of Earth Science -- geophysics, geology, and geomorphology -- provide input into morphotectonics.

A type of traditional Eastern medicine, involving the burning of an herb over certain parts of the body.
The heat therapy of moxibustion, practiced by burning moxa on or near certain joints, relieved the pain.

Relating to, producing, covered with, or the nature of mucus.
Dry mouth can result from reduced mucous secretions.

A small North Pacific seabird in the auk family.
The marbled murrelet is a threatened seabird species.

In classical mythology, a water nymph.
A naiad was said to inhabit bodies of water such as rivers, springs, or waterfalls.

Salt.
In the Indian cookbook, salt was referred to as namak.

The study of sacred buildings.
The original book on naology, written about the symbolic importance of sacred structures, had to be restored page by page because it was in such disrepair.

The bridge of the nose.
The point at the root of the nose where the frontal and two nasal bones meet is called the nasion.

Closely imitating real life or nature.
The naturalistic rock garden had manmade stones that were realistic.

The scientific study of nematodes, or round worms.
